- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing sustained upward trends.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >35.0), model underreacts or overcorrects, failing to capture continuation or reversal.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model too quickly brings prices back to “average” after spikes, ignoring structural momentum.
- Forecasts lag behind true outcomes by 1–3 days in the early part of the 30d window, especially for upward moves.
- Model underestimates volatility in late 30d window — fails to anticipate sudden drops or sharp reversals.
- When true outcome shows strong upward momentum, model forecasts remain flat or slightly upward, missing the acceleration.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent history” — forecasts too closely follow recent highs, ignoring longer-term trends.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to capture abrupt changes or “jumps” in price, especially in the last 5–10 days of the window.
